about: Thereabouts is an offline geocoder. A Parquet dataset holds the open data; binary packs built from it answer lookups through the Python, Node and command-line clients and the MCP server. This dictionary is generated from the schema file, the client code and the Rust core, so it describes exactly the tables and tools of the build that produced it.

core.answers: Reverse geocoding and city names. A latitude and longitude, or an H3 cell, gives country, subdivision, city and timezone; a town or city name gives the matching cities.
core.inputs: Coordinates in WGS84 degrees; an H3 cell of resolution 0 to 8 as 15 hexadecimal characters; a city name of at most 128 normalized characters.
core.notes: Every other family reads the core pack for city and timezone detail when it is installed. geocode finds towns and cities by canonical, English or alternate name (the names table), never street addresses.

postal.inputs: A code and the country it belongs to. Codes repeat across countries, so the country is required. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are kept.
postal.notes: One code can name several places; the result is then ambiguous with ranked candidates.

airports.inputs: A code and an optional scheme (iata, icao, gps, local or ident). Without a scheme, IATA then ICAO are searched. The local scheme needs a country.
airports.notes: Ambiguous codes return ranked candidates; a country narrows them.

locode.answers: UN/LOCODE to trade or transport location (port, airport, rail or road terminal).
locode.inputs: The five-character code (two country letters and three letters or digits), or three characters plus a country.
locode.notes: Conflicting or malformed country hints are invalid input.

phone.answers: International telephone number to the longest published calling prefix and its country.
phone.inputs: A number in E.164 form with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits; spaces, hyphens and parentheses after the plus are ignored.
phone.notes: This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation. Shared calling codes such as +1 return one candidate per country.

ip.answers: IPv4 or IPv6 address to the published geolocation interval that contains it.
ip.inputs: A bare address literal; ports, CIDR suffixes and IPv6 zones are invalid.
ip.notes: The point is the provider's location for the interval, usually a city centre, not the device.

plates.answers: Vehicle registration plate text to the countries, and sometimes the region, whose recorded formats it fits.
plates.inputs: Plate text and an optional country and series.
plates.notes: Format evidence, not a vehicle registry. Without a country the result is usually ambiguous across countries.

tools.name: reverse
tools.description:
Find the country, subdivision, city and timezone at a latitude and longitude.

Needs the core pack. status is matched when stored land covers the point
and not_found otherwise: open water, land outside the installed coverage,
or unassigned land. match says how the city was chosen: contained (inside
a boundary), nearest (nearest settlement within the distant threshold) or
nearest_distant (farther; treat the city as approximate), and
distance_band bounds that distance in kilometres. point and cell describe
the resolution 8 H3 cell that holds the input, not the input itself. With
evidence, a miss explains itself (no_land, outside_coverage, unassigned)
and a match shows the city_method that chose the city.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude in degrees, -90 to 90

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude in degrees, -180 to 180

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: h3
tools.description:
Find the stored ancestor of an H3 cell at resolution zero to eight.

Needs the core pack. Like reverse, from a cell instead of a point.
Cells of resolution 3 to 8 search themselves and their stored ancestors;
resolutions 0 to 2 have no stored ancestor and return not_found. A
resolution above 8 or a malformed cell is invalid_input.

parameters.name: cell
parameters.description: H3 cell as 15 hexadecimal characters, resolution 0 to 8

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: geocode
tools.description:
Finds towns and cities by name. Street addresses are not supported.

Needs the core pack. status is matched for one city and ambiguous when
several share the name: candidates are ranked by population and the
flat fields keep only what every candidate shares. Pass country or
subdivision to narrow them, or prefer="population" to take the largest.
match is exact, alternate_name (a published English or other name) or
fuzzy (typo tolerant; check the returned name). A street address is
unsupported_granularity.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: City or town name, not an address

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code; a hard filter

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: Subdivision code such as US-IL; a hard filter

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most candidates to return, 1 to 100

parameters.name: prefer
parameters.description: "population" picks the most populous of several cities

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: postal
tools.description:
Find a postal code in the required source country.

Needs the postal pack. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are
kept. A code that names several places is ambiguous: candidates are
ranked by population. A malformed country, such as a country name
instead of its two-letter code, is invalid_input.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code to look up; leading zeros matter

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code of the postal system

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: airport
tools.description:
Find an airport by IATA/ICAO or a specified code scheme.

Needs the airports pack. The point is the airport's own point and the
city is the canonical city around it, which can differ from the name in
the airport's title. The local scheme needs a country; an unknown scheme
is invalid_input. A code shared by several airports is ambiguous.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code to look up; leading zeros matter

parameters.name: scheme
parameters.description: iata, icao, gps, local or ident; omit for IATA then ICAO

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code; narrows ambiguous codes

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: locode
tools.description:
Find a trade location by its five-character LOCODE.

Needs the locode pack. Evidence carries the function flags, status and
remarks. A malformed code or a conflicting country is invalid_input; an
unknown code is not_found.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: UN/LOCODE, e.g. BEANR, or three characters with country

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code when the code has three characters

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: phone
tools.description:
Find the longest published prefix of an international E.164 number.

Needs the phone pack. This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation.
A calling code shared by several countries, such as +1, can be
ambiguous with one candidate per country unless country narrows it. A
number without the leading plus is invalid_input.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: E.164 number with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code; narrows a shared calling code

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: ip
tools.description:
Find published context for an IPv4 or IPv6 literal.

Needs the ip pack. The answer is the geolocation provider's location for
the interval that contains the address, usually a city centre; it is not
the location of the device. An address outside the published intervals, for
example a loopback address, is not_found.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address literal, without port or mask

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: plate
tools.description:
Find recorded registration formats, preserving country ambiguity.

Needs the plates pack. The result is format evidence, not a vehicle
registry. Without a country, plates usually fit formats of several
countries and the result is ambiguous with candidates ranked by evidence
(rank_basis). With a country the answer is that country, and evidence
explains how much geography the code supports.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Vehicle registration plate text

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country context; stays exact when given

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: Series or subdivision context for series-based plates

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources

tools.name: describe
tools.description:
Describe the open Parquet dataset behind the answers.

Without a table, lists every table with its purpose, grain, key and
number of columns. With a table, returns its columns (type, nullability,
units, meaning), primary key, joins to other tables, and the enumerated
values of coded columns. Use it before writing SQL over the dataset.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Dataset table name; omit to list every table
